title: A timed-out eval run counts as one failed run
what: A timed-out eval run counts as one failed run
why: Owner, 27 Oct, answering whether a run that did not finish in its 10 minutes is a failed run under the 2-of-3 majority rule: "7. a" (a = count it as a failed run; the summary names it; two timeouts are red). Today such a run is "not judged" and makes the whole wave red even when the other two passed. Measured 27 Oct: 22 such runs in 21 stored records, none of which would change its record's verdict. Needed before the next paid run, which plays 3 evals at once (owner, 27 Oct: "5. a"), where load may cause more timeouts. Split out of a-wave-run-is-red-when-one-of-a-case-s-3-runs-fa (review finding F5 of that change) so the majority rule lands first: relay sync waits on it.
failing_case: A case with runs PASS, PASS, timed out after 600s: the wave verdict is RED ('1 not judged').
pass_cases: PASS, PASS, timed out: green, and the summary says '2 of 3 runs passed, 1 timed out'.
PASS, timed out, timed out: red.
A falling pass rate counts a timeout as a failed run.
A test fails with the rule disabled.
